question: Which type of goal is concerned with achieving a better result than an opponent?
markScheme:
Correct answer: A - Outcome goal.
1 mark for the correct option.

question: Research shows that goal setting can have a positive effect on performance. (a) Identify the benefits of goal setting.
markScheme:
A. Improved confidence / self-efficacy
B. Increased motivation / drive
C. Prevents learning plateau
D. Task persistence / push themselves
E. Reduced anxiety / stress / more relaxed
F. Focuses attention / concentration / improved selective attention
Max 3 marks.

question: Research shows that goal setting can have a positive effect on performance. (b) Explain why a coach would use performance goals and outcome goals for a performer.
markScheme:
Performance goal:
A. To improve personal standards / personal best
(Sub max 1 mark)
B. To avoid comparisons with others
Outcome goal:
C. To achieve a better result (eg to win a game, finish in a certain position)
Max 2 marks.

question: What are outcome goals? Use a sporting example in your answer.
markScheme:
AO1:
- Outcome goals are set against the performance of others and are based on a result
AO2:
- For example, finishing on the podium in a triathlon
Accept other suitable descriptions and examples.
Max 2 marks.

question: What are task orientated goals? Use a sporting example in your answer.
markScheme:
AO1:
- Task orientated goals are concerned with improvements in technique or performance
- There are two types of task orientated goals: process and performance goals
AO2:
- For example, to improve the timing of a take-off in the long jump
Accept other suitable descriptions and examples.
Max 2 marks.

question: Identify and explain the different types of goals that a coach could use to motivate performers.
markScheme:
4 marks for 4 of:
A - SMARTER/SMART goals - specific/measurable/accepted/realistic/time phased/exciting/recorded (any two named principles for one mark)
B - Short/mid/long term goal - concept of specific goals over differing time scales (do not need to name all three to be awarded the mark)
C - Outcome/product goal - based on the end result/against other performers, eg finishing position in a race
D - Performance goal/task/task-orientated - based on personal standards, eg a personal best
E - Process-orientated goal/process goal - based on personal completion of tactics or techniques, eg completion of a specific sub-routine
(No mark for just naming types of goal.)
Max 4 marks.

question: Performers need to learn skills in order to take part in physical activity. Skilled movements are learned, economic and efficient - they do not waste energy. One way of helping performers to learn is to set suitable goals. What are the benefits of goal setting?
markScheme:
Improved confidence/self-efficacy
Increased motivation/drive
Task persistence/want to keep trying
Reduced anxiety/more relaxed or equivalent
Focuses attention/concentration/improved selective attention
Approach behaviours
Max 3 marks.

question: Effective captains use a variety of methods to motivate their teams. Explain the characteristics of effective goal setting.
markScheme:
3 marks for 3 of: (must be an explanation for each term - accept suitable examples for explanation)
(Specific) - linked to the performer/sport/position
(Measurable) - objective/not subjective
(Agreed/accepted) - involve the performer in setting the goals
(Realistic/achievable) - within the performer's ability/not demotivating
(Time phased/long and short term goals) - set a time for evaluation
(Exciting/challenging) - motivate the performer
(Recorded) - written for future reference/improves ownership (no marks for just SMART, SMARTER, SCAMP)
(Outcome goal) - based on the end result, eg winning the match
(Performance goal) - based on the performer's own ability level, eg linked to a personal best time/completing a specific percentage pass rate
(Process goal) - based on the performer's techniques/tactics, eg extending the arms when passing/completing a specific role within a tactical formation
Max 3 marks.

question: In order to improve a netball player's performance, a coach may set goals. Explain why these goals need to be realistic, specific and time-based.
markScheme:
Realistic - to maintain motivation/gain satisfaction/increase confidence by being achievable.
Specific - so the performer has personalised goals/targets for an aspect of the sport/netball.
Time-based - so the target has to be reached quickly/not too drawn out/allows evaluation/re-evaluation.
Max 3 marks.
